accent.note: Default only; overridden at runtime by the macOS accent injected as html.mx{--mx-accent}.

on-accent.note: Computed per accent at runtime: white or black, whichever contrasts more with the live macOS accent.

mark-star.note: Marked-note star badge in the reviewer, both themes; glyph colour only, never text.

large-title.purpose: One per screen: Decks, the deck name on Overview.

card.purpose: Reviewer question and answer text, centred, max 680px.

prominent.purpose: Accent capsule label; overview count values.

row.purpose: Deck names and grouped-list rows; grade labels at 600.

count.purpose: Count badges and the remaining-count line; tabular.

column-label.purpose: Column headings above the grouped list.

shadows.name: glass
shadows.purpose: Resting glass controls: toolbar groups, round buttons, mark/flag badges.

shadows.name: glass-lift
shadows.purpose: The prominent action and the reviewer answer capsule.

shadows.name: glass-rim
shadows.purpose: Specular top edge plus inner edge; stacked before glass or glass-lift on every glass control.

shadows.name: accent-rim
shadows.purpose: Specular top and faint bottom edge on accent-filled capsules.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus on every focusable element.

motion.name: ease-house
motion.purpose: Chevron rotation, deck-list entrance, answer capsule morph.

motion.name: control-feedback
motion.purpose: Hover/press background and 0.97 press scale on capsule controls (rows 100ms).

motion.name: enter
motion.purpose: Deck list rises 6px from a 3px blur; skipped under reduce-motion.

motion.name: capsule-morph
motion.value: 340ms width; segments 260ms, delay 60ms + 24ms stagger, from scale 0.94 and 4px blur
motion.purpose: Signature: Show Answer capsule morphs into the grade capsule; skipped under Anki reduce-motion or the system preference.

motion.name: backdrop
motion.purpose: Liquid Glass backdrop on glass groups and the answer capsule.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Grade segments 104px to 80px; Show Answer min width 300px to 220px.

components.css: :host{--mx-accent:#0a60ff;--mx-font:-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,"SF Pro Text","Helvetica Neue",sans-serif;--mx-ground:#f5f5f7;--mx-group:#ffffff;--mx-label:rgb(0 0 0 / 0.88);--mx-label-2:rgb(0 0 0 / 0.56);--mx-label-3:rgb(0 0 0 / 0.30);--mx-separator:rgb(0 0 0 / 0.09);--mx-fill:rgb(120 120 128 / 0.10);--mx-fill-strong:rgb(120 120 128 / 0.18);--mx-on-accent:#fff;--mx-red:#d70015;--mx-orange:#c93400;--mx-green:#1a7230;--mx-blue:#0040dd;--mx-glass:rgb(255 255 255 / 0.74);--mx-glass-hover:rgb(255 255 255 / 0.95);--mx-glass-press:rgb(232 232 236 / 0.95);--mx-glass-edge:rgb(0 0 0 / 0.08);--mx-glass-spec:rgb(255 255 255 / 0.95);--mx-glass-shadow:0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.06),0 4px 14px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.07);--mx-glass-shadow-lift:0 2px 4px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.07),0 10px 28px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.10);--mx-group-shadow:0 0 0 0.5px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.07),0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.04);font-family:var(--mx-font)} .ds-field{width:100%;max-width:480px;box-sizing:border-box;padding:8px 12px;border:none;border-radius:8px;background:var(--mx-group);box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 0.5px var(--mx-glass-edge),var(--mx-group-shadow);color:var(--mx-label);font:400 17px/1.4 var(--mx-font)}.ds-field::placeholder{color:var(--mx-label-3)}.ds-field:focus{outline:none;box-shadow:0 0 0 3.5px color-mix(in srgb,var(--mx-accent) 45%,transparent)}

narrative.overview:
Anki's main window is dressed as a first-party macOS 27 app that could sit beside Mail, Finder and System Settings. The window ground is a quiet off-white (or near-black), content lives in opaque inset grouped panels with hairline separators, and every control floats above it in Liquid Glass capsules. Nothing is decorative: depth, colour and motion all exist to say what can be pressed and what is due.

The density is Mac-native, not web-native: 13px system text, 28px capsule controls, 40 to 42px rows, a single large title per screen. Numbers are always tabular so due counts, intervals and timers line up in columns. Colour is spent almost entirely on meaning: the user's macOS accent marks the one next action and the current selection, and three state colours (new, learn, review) carry Anki's scheduling vocabulary everywhere it appears.

The system follows Anki's Light/Dark theme exactly (two complete token sets, light by default, dark under Anki's night mode) and follows the macOS accent live. It rejects Anki's stock look: a web page with a floating table and grey HTML buttons.
keyCharacteristics: Unified 52px toolbar merged with the title bar; traffic lights centred on its midline.
Liquid Glass reserved for controls; content panels are opaque.
One accent-filled capsule per screen; everything else is quiet glass or transparent.
Capsule controls, 12px grouped panels, 8px small surfaces; nothing else.
Tabular numerals wherever a number is shown.
Every bottom control sits on one centred axis shared with the reviewer's answer capsule.

rules.name: The Accent Is Live Rule
rules.body: Accent usage always goes through the accent token, never a literal blue; the user's macOS accent must repaint every accent surface without a reload.

rules.name: The Scheduling Colour Rule
rules.body: Blue, red and green mean new, learn and review (plus orange for Hard) and nothing else; zero counts drop to tertiary label instead of keeping their colour.

rules.name: The Two Sets Rule
rules.body: Every colour token has a light and a dark value; a new surface that only works in one theme is unfinished.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number (counts, intervals, timers, keycaps, statistics) is set with tabular figures so columns align.

rules.name: The One Large Title Rule
rules.body: Only the screen title uses the display weight; nothing else on the screen exceeds 15px except card content.

rules.name: The Shared Axis Rule
rules.body: Every screen's bottom control is horizontally centred so it shares one axis with the reviewer's answer capsule.

rules.name: The Glass Is For Controls Rule
rules.body: Liquid Glass (translucency, blur, specular top edge) is used only on things you can press; content panels stay opaque.

rules.name: The Soft Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are soft, neutral and stacked from a tight contact shadow and a wide diffuse one; no coloured glows, no hard offsets.

rules.name: The Three Radii Rule
rules.body: Capsule for controls, 12px for groups, 8px for small surfaces; a new radius needs a reason the build already has.

dos: **Do** route every accent use through the accent token so the macOS accent repaints it live.
**Do** keep exactly one accent-filled capsule on a screen; demote everything else to glass or transparent capsules.
**Do** put glass only on controls, and give every glass control the full recipe: translucent fill, 0.5px specular top, 0.5px edge, soft neutral shadow.
**Do** keep the answer capsule 52px tall in both states so the morph changes width, never height.
**Do** use tabular figures for every number.
**Do** draw edges as 0.5px hairlines in the separator colour.
**Do** define both light and dark values for any new colour.
**Do** gate new motion on Anki's reduce-motion class as well as the system preference.
donts: **Don't** hard-code a blue where the accent belongs.
**Don't** put glass, blur or translucency on content panels, cards or the window ground.
**Don't** use the state colours for anything but new, learn, review and the four grades.
**Don't** introduce radii outside capsule, 12px, 8px and the 5px keycap.
**Don't** use hard offset or coloured shadows.
**Don't** add a second filled accent action to a screen.
**Don't** recreate Anki's DOM nodes; restyle or move them so shortcuts, drag-and-drop and add-on links keep working.
